name: Construction of the Alhambra
summary: The Nasrid emirs of Granada began transforming the hill of the Sabika into a palace-city, the Alhambra, from the mid-13th century. The complex, completed mainly under Muhammad V (1354–1391), features the Court of the Lions, the Hall of the Abencerrajes, and the Generalife gardens. Its exquisite muqarnas ceilings, calligraphic tile-work, and sophisticated water systems represent the zenith of al-Andalus art and architecture.
outcomes: Nasrid dynasty builds palace-city on hilltop
Finest surviving example of Moorish architecture

_quarry.structural_significance: The supreme surviving monument of Islamic civilization in the Western Mediterranean; its combination of palatial architecture and garden design had no European parallel.
